To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in a motor neuronal cell model of familial amyotrophic lateral slerosis, the expression of a mutant Cu, Zn super oxide dismutase induces an alteration of glutathione synthesis, which is associated with a reduction of the flow through the Krebs cycle, with a consequent impairment of the glutamate-glutathione metabolism.

in a motor neuronal cell line model of familial ALS, the decrease in glutathione associated with mutant SUD1 is due to a mitochondrial dysfunction caused by a reduced flow of glucose-derived through the tricarboxylic acid cycle; it implies a reduced glutamate metabolism, which is dependent on different mitochondrial energy substrata.
